title: Read the control-root state in the plan-freeze fallback
action: Per D8 (issue 101). `pub(crate) fn plan_freeze_shape_approved(` in hooks/write_guard/checks.rs reads the control-root lane file first, then falls back to the `state` map it was handed — in a worktree that is the worktree's own .bee/state.json projection, which goes stale after `bee gate --merge --approved false` writes the control plane. In the fallback, read `<control_root>/.bee/state.json` (same read_json_g helper) and use its feature and approved_gates.shape; use the handed `state` when the control-root file cannot be read OR names a different feature (main may have moved on; a plan frozen per the handed state stays frozen). Red first: in hooks/write_guard/tests.rs, next to `plan_freeze_shape_approved_reads_the_default_state_when_no_lane_exists`, add a test where the control root's state.json says shape false and the handed state says shape true for the same feature, and assert false; keep the existing plan_freeze tests green (adjust fixtures that relied on the handed map only if the control root and the root are the same dir there). No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file. Add a test for the different-feature case too.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee plan_freeze && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee plan_md

truths: with no lane record, the plan freeze follows the control root state.json, not the worktree copy
when the control-root state names another feature, the handed state decides
prohibitions: No change to the lane-record path
